questions.question: What symbol shows a marine pollutant?

options.text: A bird inside a red octagon
A fish inside a white triangle with an X through it
A light blue square with a dark blue X through it

questions.correctAnswerText: A fish inside a white triangle with an X through it
questions.explanation: The marine pollutant symbol is a fish inside a white triangle with an X through it.

questions.question: Who must mark and label materials for shipping?
questions.explanation: The shipper must warn drivers and others about hazards. They do this by putting hazard labels on packages, putting placards on vehicles, and providing shipping papers and emergency information.

questions.question: Shipping papers must include:

options.text: How the materials will be used

questions.explanation: Shippers must include an emergency response telephone number on shipping papers.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that:

options.text: The package does not contain hazardous materials
The package was prepared following all rules
The package was packed at a different location

questions.correctAnswerText: The package was prepared following all rules
questions.explanation: A shipper must certify on the shipping paper that the shipment was prepared in accordance with all rules.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: How fast the material must reach its destination

questions.explanation: Materials are placed into nine classes. Each class explains the type of risks of that material.

questions.question: If your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery, turn off the engine:
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine when loading or unloading a compressed gas tank. If your engine runs a pump, turn it off after the transfer but before unhooking the hoses.

questions.question: Which sign shows that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks
questions.explanation: Packaging can show if materials are hazardous. Cylinders and drums are often used to hold and transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: What do you do if a hazardous materials label does not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag secured to the item
Attach a QR code to be scanned
Make the label smaller so it fits

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag secured to the item
questions.explanation: Put diamond-shaped hazard labels on packages. If a label will not fit on the package, place it on a tag that is securely attached to the package.

questions.question: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, use:

options.text: A certain spot in the trailer

questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label will not fit on a package, place it on a tag that is securely attached to the package.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if you need to run the engine to operate a pump. Ground the tank before opening it and keep it grounded until after closing.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty cargo tanks used for hazardous materials, you must:

options.text: Slow down at a railroad crossing, but you don't have to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop before crossing railroad tracks if your vehicle has cargo tanks for hazardous materials. This applies whether the tanks are full or empty.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while transporting explosives, warn other drivers with:

options.text: By standing on the roadway and waving your arms.

questions.explanation: Use reflective triangles or red electric lights for warning signals. Never use flares or other burning signals when transporting explosives—they are a fire hazard.

questions.question: If you find hazardous materials leaking while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving to find a phone and call the National Response Center.
Leave the area to find help.

questions.explanation: Park the vehicle as soon as possible. Continuing to drive spreads the leak, creating more danger and increasing cleanup costs.

questions.question: What must you have in your vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: You must have an approved gas mask in your vehicle when transporting chlorine in cargo tanks.

questions.question: Shipping papers for hazardous materials must include:

options.text: The location of fire departments on your route.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must list an emergency response telephone number.

questions.question: A hazardous material's identification number must appear:

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the shipping paper and on the packaging. It must also be on cargo tanks and other bulk containers.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, you need to know that:

options.text: Radiation spreads outward and passes through nearby packages.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads outward and passes through nearby packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from each package and passes through to all nearby packages. Rules limit how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling materials correctly. The driver should check that materials are properly labeled.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, you need:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to operate any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: You should not smoke within ____ of a vehicle marked with Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (flammable gases). Never smoke or carry a lit cigarette, cigar, or pipe near vehicles with flammable or explosive materials.

questions.question: Load hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Rules prevent flammable or explosive materials from being loaded in cargo areas with heaters.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank open during loading and unloading. Close them at all other times.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should not be:

options.text: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
Parked within 40 feet of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Do not park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building, except for brief stops for vehicle operations. Never park within 5 feet of the road.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees receive training?

options.text: At least once every three years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years
questions.explanation: Employees who work with hazardous materials must receive training and pass a test at least once every three years.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a hazardous materials shipping paper, the paper must also show:

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous materials.
The type of packaging containing the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: A "G" in Column 1 means the description in Column 2 is a generic name. Generic shipping names must be followed by the technical name.

questions.question: On a shipping paper with both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials may be identified by:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials on a mixed shipping paper must be clearly identified. You can list them first, highlight them in a different color, or mark them with an "X" before the shipping description.

questions.question: A hazardous materials placard must be placed:

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the outside of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, a driver needs:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a tank endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: Hazardous materials shipping papers may be:

options.text: Kept in a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Kept in a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another easily accessible location while you are wearing your seat belt. Papers must be visible to anyone entering the cab.
